meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with why my son's mark changed before anyone called me.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen asked a single question before it went in?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. Owen told me he wrote that essay over the weekend, so turn the screen and let me read that history myself, with the dates. Who else has seen it?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing down "That line is not in Hamlet." Hand me the text and I'll search it myself, and I still haven't seen that version history. Did anyone ask Owen about either one before the zero went in?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's procedure 4.4, and I printed it before I came in. I want the zero off the gradebook today, a written promise that nothing goes on his record, and no one in his class told a thing. Then I'll look at "Thursday at 8:15", after I've read those two documents myself.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, a written promise that nothing goes on Owen's record, no one in his class told anything, and a look at the version history and the Hamlet text myself. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position, still wanting the zero off the gradebook today, a written promise of nothing on his record, and no one in his class told, with the Thursday rewrite not yet accepted until she has seen both documents.
What moved her: "612 words arrive in one edit", because it was specific, timed and tied to Owen's own essay, and it got her writing down times and asking real questions.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked you to turn the screen for the version history, show it to her right then, before moving on to the quotation and the rewrite offer.
